correctness.summary: Faraco--Rungi's global geometrization theorem makes the minimum finite; their parity obstruction and holonomy-preserving bubbling imply that every total degree of the correct parity at or above the minimum is realized and no other degree is. Fixed-signature holonomy images are open, so exact-degree and minimal-degree sublevel loci are open. The integer-valued minimum is therefore upper semicontinuous. Every nonempty open set contains a nonempty open region where the minimum attains its least value on that set, proving an open dense locally constant locus. Boundary points of the sublevel sets are exactly the jump points. Compact families admit finitely many fixed signatures by a finite-subcover argument.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The current Faraco--Rungi preprint formulates minimal branching degree for non-Hitchin representations and proves the ingredients used here, but no saturated total-degree spectrum theorem, upper-semicontinuity statement, open-dense local-constancy result, closed nowhere-dense jump-locus description, or compact finite-signature-bank theorem was located. Le Fils computes the analogous minimum in the complex-projective setting and uses degree-raising surgeries, but no matching semicontinuity or local-constancy statement was located there. The motivating preprint is extremely recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations remain a residual risk.

value.summary: The result completely determines the coarse total-degree realization spectrum once the still-unknown minimum is known, and it gives the unknown invariant a strong deformation-theoretic structure: upper semicontinuity, generic local constancy, a closed nowhere-dense jump set, and finite signature control on compact representation families. These conclusions organize the open minimal-degree problem without claiming to solve prescribed-signature realization.

limitations: The result does not compute the minimal branching degree for non-Hitchin representations.
It does not solve prescribed-signature realization; only total branching degree is classified.
No effective upper bound, neighborhood radius, or description of the jump locus is obtained.
The motivating preprint is very recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations may overlap.
